reaction: The distinction between conserving and replacing water is clear and useful.
reason: Drinking water is the only offered combination and should show replacement.
expectation: I expect drinking water to enter the digestive tract and be absorbed into the body, though the result may require another step.

effect: Drinking water is absorbed into circulation, and the inset shows the water-control response easing gradually as plasma becomes less concentrated. Both goals are complete.
reaction: The distinction between intestinal absorption and the separate urine route is useful; the feedback inset also closes the loop.

mostWorthwhile.text: Water loss producing more collecting-duct channels was the most worthwhile construction: it connects hormonal control to water recovery and distinguishes conservation from replacement.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the sensing circuit to the pituitary was a fairly predictable assembly step, although its explanation of the nerve-to-blood signal was useful.

surprise.text: The final picture showed the response easing gradually after drinking, rather than simply showing water entering the body.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, but the initial brain-circuit construction did not explain how sensing changes ADH activity; that connection became clearer through later results.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: linking a familiar act like drinking to hormones, kidney channels and feedback made the system interesting, though the compatible-options menu made the assembly choices fairly guided.
